name: dft.cost_per_candidate
unit: core-h per candidate (one DFT stability check)
source_passage_or_derivation: A span, not a point. Low: our first-hand estimate at the base size (18 atoms), from the dft.scf_* and dft.ionic_steps records below (QE 6.7, PBE, GBRV ultrasoft, 4 ranks on an ARM64 laptop; the fit gives 3.59 at 20 atoms, where the raw measured median is 3.77 -- CHANGED 2026-10-18, this note quoted the measured 3.77 as though it were the fitted value). High: Materials Project, 1-5 calculations per material at ~200 CPU-h each (https://www.nersc.gov/assets/Uploads/NERSCuserday-jain.pdf). Base: geometric midpoint sqrt(low x high), a convention; the span covers more than two orders of magnitude, so stage 2 should sample it log-uniformly. Both provenance points are kept as the cross-check records dft.mp_2012_* below.

name: dft.wrong_verdict_chemistry_cells
unit: cross-functional flip rate within a composition cell at fixed element count
source_passage_or_derivation: COMPANION ANALYSIS BY THIS AUTHOR, not yet public. A chemistry-resolved audit of the same GNoME r2SCAN recompute (139,541 rows of DeepMind's stable_materials_r2scan.csv) finds a global flip rate of 13.04% against the MP hull, reproducing the published 86.8% quaternary survival. Holding element count fixed, disjoint composition cells run from 4.0% [3.48, 4.54] for intermetallics with no lanthanide or 3d element (n = 5,025) to 30.7% [28.97, 32.57] for oxides with a 3d element and no lanthanide (n = 2,478), a 26.7 pp spread across 23 cells at n_elements = 4. ADDED 2026-10-11. Used ONLY as a reported range on level-1 cost, never as a base value: the base of this record is the companion's global rate and the stage-1 base remains dft.wrong_verdict_frac. STANDING: the companion is unposted at the time of writing, so the range is attributed in the text as work in preparation rather than cited as published. It widens the paper's reported uncertainty rather than narrowing it, so using an unrefereed own result here is conservative; it should be replaced by a citation once the companion is public, and the direction of the change checked if its numbers move in review.

name: dft.wrong_verdict_frac
unit: fraction of DFT-stable verdicts that are wrong
source_passage_or_derivation: PROXY: a disagreement rate between two levels of theory, NOT experimental failure. No source we found reports a direct error rate against experiment. No PUBLISHED source we found breaks the flip rate down by chemistry -- only by number of elements -- but one does exist: the companion analysis recorded in dft.wrong_verdict_chemistry_cells, by this author and unposted at the time of writing, resolves the same recompute by chemistry and finds 4.0% to 30.7% across cells at fixed element count. CHANGED 2026-10-18: this note previously denied that any chemistry breakdown existed, which the companion contradicts. The paper's Section 3.4 had already been corrected; the note had not, so results/parameter_manifest.csv was shipping a claim the manuscript disowns. Base 0.16 and low 0.132, both PUBLISHED and both verified 2026-10-11: GNoME reports that '84% of the discovered binaries and ternary materials also present negative phase-separation energies' and '86.8% of tested quaternaries also remain stable on the r2SCAN convex hull', i.e. 16% and 13.2% flip. Note these are two different tests, not one metric split by arity: phase-separation energy for the binaries and ternaries, r2SCAN hull position for the quaternaries. High 0.3434 is DERIVED and more loosely comparable than base and low. An et al. 2026 (arXiv:2607.01713) report that of 166 DYNAMICALLY STABLE candidates, 109 (65.7%) have an E_SCAN_hull below 1 meV/atom; 57/166 = 34.3% is our subtraction, and the paper does not call it a flip rate. Two caveats follow: SCAN was not run on the 132 candidates eliminated earlier, so this is not a PBE->SCAN flip rate over all 298 PBE-stable materials, and the population is pre-screened on dynamical stability, which the other two endpoints are not. CHANGED 2026-10-11: the note previously described the An et al. figure as a PBE->SCAN flip rate with 109 of 166 surviving, which overstated what the source states. A-Lab's own attribution, for context only: 3 of 16 analysed failures were computational.

name: novelty.science_frac
unit: fraction of synthesised, database-novel targets that are new to science
source_passage_or_derivation: NO PUBLISHED NONZERO COUNT WAS FOUND for this campaign, within the search scope the paper states. Leeman et al. state that 'none of the materials produced by A-lab were new', and that the three they regard as correctly synthesised -- MnAgO2, Y3In2Ga3O12, CaFe2(PO4)2O -- 'have been reported'. The A-Lab correction makes no new-to-science claim: 'new to the platform, not necessarily new to science' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12872444). So every value here but the low one is a statistical bound on a zero count, not a count. Low 0.0 = the published verdict. Base 0.0964 = Wilson 95% upper bound on 0 of 36. High 0.1556 = Wilson 99% upper bound on the same. Both bounds make cost per NEW material optimistic, since a higher novelty share divides the cost. CHANGED 2026-10-11: high was 0.25, derived as '9/36 not attributed to known or disordered phases' by subtracting Leeman's error categories from 36. That subtraction is invalid -- the categories OVERLAP by construction ('Compounds can have several errors'): very poor fit 18/36, prediction changed to match 8/36, no evidence of predicted ordering 24/36, already reported 3/36, summing to 53. Leeman report that 35 of the 36 carry at least one error type, so the residual is 1, not 9, and that one is CaFe2(PO4)2O, which they class as already reported. Verified against the PRX Energy text 2026-10-11.

source_passage_or_derivation: Azoulay, Gross & Sampat (2025), 'Indirect Cost Recovery in U.S. Innovation Policy', NBER WP 33627. Base: the EFFECTIVE indirect cost recovery (ICR) rate, what NIH actually pays, averages 42% (abstract; Table 1, 2024: mean 42%, median 40%, s.d. 10%, min 14%, max 81%). High: the NEGOTIATED ICR rate, the ceiling an institution may charge, averages 58% (abstract; Table 1, 2024: mean 58%, median 56%). Low: 'effective rates in practice are generally between 25% and 45%' (section 3.3, p. 17), lower end. Applying the negotiated 58% would overstate indirect cost by about a third. Population: the underlying data are NIH indirect-cost records for 354 NIH grantee institutions (69% universities, 18% independent hospitals, 13% research institutes; NIH RePORTER since 2006 and the CGAF before), not a census of US universities. The effective rate is NIH ICR paid divided by direct costs for the institution as a whole, a total-direct-cost denominator, whereas the model applies it to an MTDC-like base that excludes tuition and service fees; on a narrower base the true rate per base dollar is somewhat higher, so 42% leans low. Vocabulary: the paper's headline term is 'indirect cost recovery'; it uses 'F&A rate' only for the negotiated agreement. Used only when cost_basis = funder. Base of the charge: labour, fringe, crucibles, precursors and other consumables (MTDC includes salaries, fringe, materials, supplies and services and excludes tuition remission, 2 CFR 200.1, https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/2/200.1). XRD and furnace recharge fees are left out of the base by default: service-centre rates 'must normally consist of its direct costs and an allocable share of all indirect costs' (2 CFR 200.468(b)(2), https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/2/200.468), so indirect cost on top would double-count. Institutional practice varies; choices.fa_base_includes_service_fees reverses this. Negotiated-rate examples, not used: Caltech FY2026 on-campus 70% (https://www.fundingopportunities.caltech.edu/static/guides/FY26_Rate_Memo.pdf), Stanford 54% (FY2025-26), Michigan 56% (FY2025-29), MIT 62% (FY2026). The 2025 NIH 15% cap was vacated (First Circuit, Jan 2026) and is not used.

name: synth.labour_annual_salary
source_passage_or_derivation: PAIRING: a graduate trainee's cost with trainee throughput (synth.labour_attempts_per_week, Liverpool undergraduate researchers), the closest wage-paid role with a sourced rate. NIH NRSA predoctoral stipend FY2026, 29,364. Not used: postdoc 63,480-77,076 (same notice), because no source we found gives postdoc throughput for manual solid-state synthesis; a postdoc at trainee throughput would mix roles.

name: synth.labour_attempts_per_week
source_passage_or_derivation: Liverpool manual solid-state, authors' estimate 10-20 per undergraduate researcher; base = midpoint (derived). A composition is taken as one recipe attempt.

name: synth.labour_fringe_rate
source_passage_or_derivation: Stanford FY2026 graduate assistant fringe, 7.5% (matches the trainee pairing; postdoc rate 27.4% not used).

name: synth.labour_tuition_remission
unit: USD per year charged for the trainee's tuition
source_passage_or_derivation: No national average for tuition remission on research grants was found. Base (proxy): NRSA predoctoral tuition allowance cap, 60% of tuition up to 16,000/yr (NOT-OD-26-044 as summarised by UCSD). High (derived): NIH caps graduate salary + fringe + tuition at the zero-year postdoc stipend, 63,480 (NOT-OD-17-003, https://grants.gatech.edu/sites/default/files/documents/main/nih_graduate_student_salary_cap_01-2018.pdf), leaving 63,480 - 29,364 x 1.075 = 31,914. Low 0: trainee on a fellowship that pays tuition. Excluded from F&A (not in MTDC).

name: synth.other_consumables_per_attempt
source_passage_or_derivation: A-Lab lists its consumables as 'plastic vials, ZrO2 balls and crucibles' and mixes with ethanol and 'ten 5-mm ZrO2 balls'; no costs are published. Base (derived, Fisher US list prices): ethanol 1 mL (ASTRAL robot volume, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2304.00743) at $267.50/L = 0.27; three weighing dishes at $147.50/500 = 0.89; one pair of nitrile gloves at $27.75/100 = 0.56; ten 5-mm YSZ balls, 3.93 g at density 6.0 g/cm3 (assumption) and $246.50/250 g = 3.87 if single use. Low: balls reused, 1.71. High (assumption): 25, for the unpriced items: plastic vials, glovebox consumables for air-sensitive work, agate mortar wear, sieves. XRD sample holders are reused (A-Lab SI) and not charged.

name: synth.precursor_mass_g_per_attempt
unit: g of precursor mix per attempt
source_passage_or_derivation: No source we found gives a per-attempt mass; A-Lab says only 'multigram sample quantities' (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10700133). Base (proxy): ~1.5 g manual samples (Na-superionic paper, SI). Low (proxy): 'nominal 0.5 g sample' in the Precursor Genome air-sensitivity test (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.09903); XRD needs > 100 mg (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.29344). High (assumption): 5 g as an upper reading of 'multigram'. Unverified, not used: DASH thesis 'up to 1.8 g'.

name: synth.precursor_usd_per_g
unit: USD per g of stoichiometric precursor mix
source_passage_or_derivation: Derived by src/derive.py from Fisher Scientific US list prices fetched 2026-10-10 (catalogue numbers and URLs in the CSV; USD, visible without login; contract prices may be lower) and the routes in data/precursors/routes.csv for our six compositions. Per target, precursors are mixed in stoichiometric mass. Low: cheapest target (Li2MnSiO4) at the largest pack. Base: the MEDIAN OVER the six targets' blended prices at the smallest pack of >= 100 g, which for an even count is the mean of the two middle blends (TiSiN2 1.3503 and NaMnF3 2.1703, giving 1.7603) -- so no single target has this value. CHANGED 2026-10-18 -- this said 'median target', which reads as one target's blend. High: dearest target (BaTiS3) at the smallest pack. Rare and transition-metal precursors dominate: In2O3 5.92-10.95 $/g, BaS 10.70-12.80, MnF2 2.96-5.11, against ZnO 0.06-0.33 and Li2CO3 0.37-0.82. The TiSiN2 and BaTiS3 routes are cost proxies (no TiN or TiS2 price). Sigma-Aldrich (A-Lab's supplier) blocked fetching. Not modelled: buying a whole pack for a few grams, which raises cost per attempt for small campaigns.

name: synth.recipe_budget
unit: maximum recipes tried per target (budget model)
source_passage_or_derivation: Derived from two A-Lab figures with a budget model: each recipe succeeds with probability q, a target gets at most B recipes, so per-target success s = 1 - (1 - q)^B and expected recipes = s / q. A-Lab's s = 36/57 and 353/57 = 6.19 recipes per target give q = 0.102 and B = 9.29. Used by the Monte Carlo and scenarios to tie recipes to success (correlation recipes_vs_success); the deterministic base case keeps A-Lab's observed 6.19.

name: synth.recipes_per_target
source_passage_or_derivation: CAMPAIGN-REPORTED multiplicity, not a derived quantity. BASE 1.0: Prein et al. (arXiv:2511.01790) attempted each of 24 targets once -- the middle reading, which the deterministic base case follows, so the base case is now one campaign throughout rather than Prein's success rate paired with A-Lab's recipe budget. HIGH 6.193: A-Lab. CHANGED 2026-10-11 (second change today): base was 6.193, which charged the middle reading about eight recipes per target for a campaign that reports one. A-Lab detail, VERIFIED against both versions. The CORRECTED article prints 353 recipes and 57 targets: 353/57 = 6.193, the base. The ORIGINAL 2023 article prints 355 recipes and 58 targets (eScholarship qt4w49b5cb): 355/58 = 6.1207, the low. The 355 -> 353 change is silent -- the Author Correction notice never mentions the recipe count -- so both pairings are defensible and the range spans them. CHANGED 2026-10-11: high was 6.228 = 355/57, which paired the ORIGINAL numerator with the CORRECTED denominator. That is a cross-version splice and was never a real reading; the original pairing is LOWER than the corrected one, so the alternative is a low endpoint, not a high one.

name: synth.success_multiplier_mlip_filtered
unit: multiplier on synthesis success for pipelines B and C only
source_passage_or_derivation: Sensitivity switch, default 1 (success does not depend on how a candidate was found). No source in sources/ measures this. The expected direction is above 1: MLIPs are trained on Materials Project data, mostly synthesised materials, so a pre-filter plausibly selects more synthesisable candidates. base_case.py reports the value needed for a 2x level-2 spread.

name: synth.success_unconditional
unit: fraction of targets made as the target phase (unconditional, as the campaign reports it)
source_passage_or_derivation: UNCONDITIONAL rates throughout, as each campaign reports them. Base: Prein et al. 2025, 7/24 = 0.29167 unconditional (24 targets attempted; 8 fused to their crucibles and could not be characterised; 7 of the remaining 16 formed the target phase). CHANGED 2026-10-11: was 7/16 = 0.4375, which conditions on a characterisable product and so was not comparable with the other two readings, both of which count against targets attempted. High: A-Lab corrected, 36/57 = 0.6316 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10700133). Low: Leeman et al. 2024, 3/58 = 0.05172 (https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10532478). Other: Prein 7/24 = 29% counting uncharacterisable; Chen et al. 2024, 1/4. CHANGED 2026-10-11: was 'given the DFT verdict is right', with high = 38/54 = 0.7037 (computational failures removed from the denominator AND the two manual-intervention successes added) and the model then dividing all three readings by (1 - w). Only the optimistic reading had been conditioned, so the middle and pessimistic branches were charged computational failure twice. All three are now unconditional and (1 - w) no longer enters the synthesis pass rate. The A-Lab target-level crosswalk is still PENDING, so 36/57 is a proposed baseline, not a settled count.

name: synth.weeks_per_year
source_passage_or_derivation: Calendar weeks; spreads annual pay over all weeks, so it slightly understates the cost per working week.

name: synth.xrd_cost_per_sample
source_passage_or_derivation: Base: UT Austin internal service, 80 USD/sample. High: UT Austin external, 150. Low: Oregon State self-use, 5 USD per 30-min slot (https://xrd.science.oregonstate.edu/fees). LOWER BOUND on resource cost: recharge fees do not fully cover shared-facility costs (Strom et al. 2020, MRS Bulletin 45(5) 331-335; claim not yet checked against the article text).
